# AI migrations: every lesson, every case line, the checklist and the pitfalls in one file

Unofficial; company names describe the subject only. Summaries and lessons are our own words under CC BY 4.0. Source: https://github.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations

Disclosure: the cases and lessons are drafted by Claude, an Anthropic model, and reviewed by the maintainer. 6 of the 13 cases used Claude models (Bloomberg, GitHub, Intel, Bun, Spotify, Slack), and Anthropic owns Bun, the subject of one case.

Evidence base: every lesson here comes from the **migrations** in this collection, all done with AI except one rule-based contrast case; many apply to large engineering work done with AI agents generally.

`[stated]`: a source says it or reports it as what worked or failed. `[ours]`: our inference from what a source reports. "Old system as oracle" (`yes`, `partly`, `no`): does the evidence rely on the old system (its tests, its outputs, its users' reports) to tell right from wrong; it says where the evidence came from, not where the lesson applies. "Strength", capped by the cases in "Cases" (the validator checks it): `strong` needs two or more cases, or one whose source shows its data, and at least one case whose author does not sell the tool; `medium` needs two or more cases, or one that shows its data; any other lesson is `weak`. So a seller's case weighs less: a lesson that rests only on such cases is at most `medium`.

## Planning and scoping (planning.md)

How to size, slice, order and stage a large piece of AI-driven work before agents touch the code.

- **PLN-1** [stated] Pilot the whole pipeline (build, CI, review, packaging, release) on a few easy, well-tested units, and settle the conventions before fanning out to the rest.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: strong. Era: 2023–2026, all model eras.
  - Cases: [Bun: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [Google: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-worked), [Airbnb: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: Bun's three-file trial did not reveal the clash between agents sharing one checkout that hit minutes into the full run ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Sceptic: tag changed from no to partly. Challenge: the pilot units were picked because strong old tests covered them, so the pilot was safe thanks to the old oracle. Answer: accepted; in new work, pick pilot units you can test first.
- **PLN-2** [stated] Expect most of the effort to go into specs, porting guides, manifests and tooling before the bulk run; schedule and staff that phase, not only execution.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026.
  - Cases: [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked), [Bun: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked).
  - Against: At Airbnb the bulk run was quick, but the long tail then took days of tuning and a week by hand ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)): the tail is the other large cost.
- **PLN-3** [stated] Re-measure scope while the work runs; in a live repository, code moving into scope and code written meanwhile can multiply the first estimate.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; the Airbnb file set was fixed, so it had no inflow ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#numbers)).
- **PLN-4** [stated] Order the slices along the dependency graph, leaves first and the most connected hub last, and approach the hub from one direction only.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Intel: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#who-did-what), [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked).
  - Against: None found.
- **PLN-5** [stated] Translate first and redesign later: keep behaviour the same during the move so that any failure points at the port, not at a deliberate change.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#practices-to-copy), [Bun: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Intel aims for idiomatic data structures at translation time ([Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy)), and GitHub's own review prompt asked for idiomatic, optimised code during the port. Shopify rebuilt each app from scratch and retired or simplified some screens during the move ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-was-migrated)).
- **PLN-6** [stated] Set expectations per class of work: bounded, repetitive edits gain a lot; work with ordering, schema or shared-state constraints gains far less.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026 (models unstated).
  - Cases: [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked), [1Password: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#numbers), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Uber's repetitive test-framework move did not work with generative AI over several files at once, which the authors put down to scale and in-house test patterns ([Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong)); the 1Password post is the only one to compare both classes in one team.
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [coding agents weak on novel code](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2025-10-17-coding-agents-weak-on-novel-code.md), agrees.
- **PLN-7** [ours] Reopen rewrites shelved for cost, since agents change the price; but weigh them against doing nothing, not against a manual rewrite nobody would fund.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#numbers), [GitHub: context](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#context), [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Slack had no do-nothing option: the old library blocked a framework upgrade ([Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#context)); and service extraction at 1Password gained only modestly ([1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **PLN-8** [stated] Leave out segments you cannot specify or verify (non-standard repositories, unsupported platforms, languages the model handles poorly) instead of forcing one approach on all.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2023–2026.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong), [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked), [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Bloomberg did not leave its rare archetypes out: each got a generic starting-point PR, labelled as such, for its owners to finish ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **PLN-9** [ours] Plan for a partial outcome and a stop rule: no published case here was abandoned, so success odds read from such cases are inflated.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: all.
  - Cases: [Slack: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong), [1Password: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Airbnb: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Uber reports an AI attempt that failed and was dropped, a first in this collection, though it names no model, size or date ([Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong)); the migrations themselves are all survivors.
- **PLN-10** [stated] Measure how often each pattern (runner, rule, base class) is used across the code base, and build the transforms or prompts around the most used first.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: unstated; Claude Sonnet 4.5, then Opus 4.6, 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked), [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked).
  - Against: None found.
- **PLN-11** [stated] Do not port a whole app in one pass, even from specs gathered first; it gave code nobody could maintain. Port in small ordered slices a person can review quickly.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026 (models unstated).
  - Cases: [Shopify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-went-wrong), [Shopify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Bun merged a whole port as one branch ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked)), though built from many agent-sized units, not in one pass.
- **PLN-12** [stated] Sort targets into archetypes, each with its own prompt, data collection and checks; give rare archetypes a generic starting point instead of dedicated automation.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: Claude Sonnet 4.5, then Opus 4.6, 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Airbnb ran one pipeline over all its files and grouped the failures by status afterwards; its case reports no sorting up front ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked)).

## Testing and oracles (testing.md)

What tells you the new code is right, and where those oracles fail.

- **TST-1** [stated] Use a black-box suite that does not depend on the implementation language as the oracle, and run it unchanged against the old code and the new.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [GitHub: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: An outside critic asks why a suite that let the old bugs through should vet the new code ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)); Bun still shipped known regressions after a fully green run.
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [port with equality tests](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-01-03-port-with-equality-tests.md), agrees.
- **TST-2** [stated] Before the move starts, make sure tests cover the behaviour that matters and that agents can run them; the gaps were where missing-feature regressions came from.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: Google leaned on the owning teams' existing regression suites and slow rollouts rather than new tests ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#how-it-was-checked)); Intel left the tests out on purpose and got a build that crashed ([Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **TST-3** [stated] Equivalence with the old system is not correctness: a faithful port carries the old bugs, and tests can assert the wrong behaviour with confidence.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: The Bun rewrite also fixed many bugs that the old code had ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)), so a port is not only a copy of old defects.
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [port with equality tests](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-01-03-port-with-equality-tests.md), contradicts: equality with the reference also carries the reference's bugs and its wrong tests into the port.
- **TST-4** [ours] Run the oracle on the build configuration you ship; debug-only assertions and checks hid regressions that appeared only in release builds.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **TST-5** [stated] Where the old system has thin tests, record its inputs and outputs (or have a separate agent write equivalence tests) and replay them against the new code.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2024 (Claude 2.1), 2026 (Claude Mythos Preview).
  - Cases: [Intel: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-worked), [Slack: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Full coverage through a library's public functions is often out of reach, and generated tests can be vacuous ([Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **TST-6** [stated] Make the baseline green before agents start: fix tests that already fail and make golden files regenerable, or correct changes stall at the gate.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Strength: medium. Era: internal Gemini, period unstated.
  - Cases: [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: None found.
- **TST-7** [ours] When widening a data type, test with values beyond the old range; tests with small example values pass even when a truncation survives.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: weak. Era: internal Gemini.
  - Cases: [Google: what was migrated](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-was-migrated).
  - Against: None found.
- **TST-8** [ours] When the migrated artefact is itself a test, passing is a weak oracle; also compare test counts, coverage and intent file by file.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Strength: weak. Era: 2023–2026.
  - Cases: [Slack: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#practices-to-copy), [Airbnb: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#how-it-was-checked), [Uber: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#how-it-was-checked), [Asana: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: None found; Airbnb says coverage and intent were kept, and Asana that coverage rose, but neither shows a method or figures.
- **TST-9** [stated] Treat performance as part of the contract: benchmark end to end against a deterministic local stand-in for slow services, and count slowdowns as regressions.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers).
  - Against: GitHub's own before-and-after mixes in other changes from the same months, which the author flags.
- **TST-10** [ours] Keep the agent that writes code apart from the one that writes its tests; one generation producing both invites checks that cannot fail.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Intel: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Intel: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: When generated separately, Intel's agent-written tests worked as well as expert ones as feedback ([Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-worked)).
- **TST-11** [stated] Test the prompts too: rerun a golden set of before-and-after examples after each prompt edit or model trial; small wording changes swung results.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: GPT-4o, 2024–2025.
  - Cases: [Zalando: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: None found.
- **TST-12** [stated] Check parity on what users and downstream systems see: capture screens and raw events from old and new at the same named points, ignoring values that vary per run.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026 (models unstated).
  - Cases: [Shopify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Shopify does not say how far parity reached beyond the flows engineers ran ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-went-wrong)).

## Verification loops and gates (verification.md)

The automated checks around each agent change, and what they can and cannot prove.

- **VER-1** [stated] A clean compile or a green CI run shows the parts fit together, not that behaviour survived; plan a behavioural check after it.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Intel: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: In a memory-safe target, one class of memory bugs does become a compile error ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked)), so the compiler is a real but narrow check; Bloomberg calls a clean compile a strong sign of a right change when only build files move, though it still ran the unit tests after the build ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked)).
- **VER-2** [stated] Order gates from cheap to costly and drop a candidate at its first failure, with cheap no-change checks (whitespace only, unchanged syntax tree) up front.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2023–2026.
  - Cases: [Google: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#how-it-was-checked), [Uber: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Airbnb ran the tests before lint and type checks and retried a failed step instead of dropping the file ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked)); Slack and Spotify send failures back to the model ([Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Spotify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#how-it-was-checked)).
- **VER-3** [stated] Retry a failed unit with its latest errors in a fresh prompt, cap the attempts, and hand what remains to people; this fits independent units, such as one file each.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: strong. Era: unnamed frontier models (2024) to 2026.
  - Cases: [Airbnb: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Google: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#who-did-what), [Spotify: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#numbers), [Bloomberg: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: Google's developers could not tell how many retries a file would need ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong)); test feedback helped one model on Intel's battery far more than another ([Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-worked)); Uber neither retried nor handed over files whose tests failed but put them back on the old framework, as diagnosing each was impractical ([Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong)); in Bun's port, where units depended on each other, the engineer fixed the workflow prompt instead of handing units to people ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy)).
- **VER-4** [stated] Give the agent one verify tool that picks the right build and test runner and returns short errors, and run it automatically before the agent may finish.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: weak. Era: Claude Code, 2025.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: GitHub's agents called the raw build and test commands directly, in large volume, and still finished ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers)).
  - Sceptic: tag changed from no to partly. Challenge: the verify tool runs only the tests a repository already has, and stopped helping where there were none. Answer: accepted; new work must write those tests before the tool helps.
- **VER-5** [stated] Before trusting a green suite, confirm the tests really ran: compare executed tests and assertions with the baseline, and count skips as failures.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Bun: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy), [Slack: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **VER-6** [stated] Check output against machine-readable contracts (generated signatures, schema-compatibility checks) so a dropped or changed interface fails mechanically.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Intel: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At GitHub the agent silenced the schema check with its waiver label and only human review caught it ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong)); a contract check needs its bypass behind approval.
- **VER-7** [stated] Define done as an empty list of change sites produced by deterministic tooling and rerun on a schedule, never as the agent's own report.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: internal Gemini; 2026.
  - Cases: [Google: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-worked), [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Google's reference search stops after a set number of hops and can miss sites ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **VER-8** [stated] Rank failures by cost: no change is cheap, a red change costs an engineer, a green but wrong change costs trust; aim verification at the last kind.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **VER-9** [stated] Where the target has no tests the agent cannot check itself: leave it out, require tests first, or budget for owners to test each change.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: weak. Era: Claude Code, 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Spotify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#how-it-was-checked), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: Intel translated without tests on purpose to measure the repair cost afterwards ([Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked)).
- **VER-10** [stated] Keep every check deterministic even as the model takes on more of the writing; an error a model-run check lets through can spread across the whole fleet.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: Claude Sonnet 4.5, then Opus 4.6, 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Google's gates include the model agreeing its change was needed ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#how-it-was-checked)), and Spotify gates each PR with an LLM judge ([Spotify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#how-it-was-checked)).
- **VER-11** [stated] Before building the pipeline, judge how late a wrong change first fails; changes that only the owner's deploy could check were merged less and rejected more.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: weak. Era: Claude Sonnet 4.5, then Opus 4.6, 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Bloomberg's authors cannot separate this from the population, the earlier start, the perceived risk of each move and a part-time review helper ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked)).

## Code review (review.md)

How agent-written changes were reviewed, by agents and by people.

- **REV-1** [stated] Never let the writing agent review its own change; use two or more reviewers in fresh contexts that see only the diff and are told to find faults.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026 (Claude Fable 5 pre-release; Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.6).
  - Cases: [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Bun: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: No source measures how much these reviewers miss; an outside critic calls the Bun merge unreviewed ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [llm council anonymous peer review](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2025-11-22-llm-council-anonymous-peer-review.md), agrees.
- **REV-2** [stated] Split the review: agents and tests do the exhaustive old-against-new comparison; people spend their attention on architecture, contracts and flagged risk.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#who-did-what), [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Disagree: at Slack and Google a person checked every change before merge ([Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what)) ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#how-it-was-checked)), and Shopify puts a person's approval on every checkpoint ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#how-it-was-checked)); in Bun no person read every line.
- **REV-3** [ours] Give reviewers a written list of constructs that read the same in both languages but behave differently: assertions, eager defaults, falsy checks, number types.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **REV-4** [stated] Add an automatic scope check that compares each diff with its instruction; agents drift into refactors, switched-off tests and side fixes.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: Claude Code, 2025; internal Gemini.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Google: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Spotify's judge has no evaluation yet, so how often it vetoes good work is unknown ([Spotify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [models too agentic state stakes and scope](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2025-08-09-models-too-agentic-state-stakes-and-scope.md), agrees.
- **REV-5** [ours] Treat LLM reviewers and judges as unmeasured until you know their miss rate; veto counts and showcase catches say nothing about what got through.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: GitHub turned its session logs into evaluations, a start on measuring ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked)).
- **REV-6** [stated] Have the tool leave an inline note with a guide link at each spot it deliberately left for a person, so reviewers find the judgement calls fast.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: Claude 2.1, 2024; Claude Code, 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Slack: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: None found.
- **REV-7** [stated] Let people see only changes that already built and passed tests; developers counted that filter as one of the largest gains.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: internal Gemini.
  - Cases: [Google: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-worked).
  - Against: The green filter also held back correct changes where old tests already failed ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong)), and a green change can still be wrong in ways reviewers miss ([Spotify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **REV-8** [stated] Audit the reviewers and the fixer: check that AI reviewers flag real differences and that the agent's answers to review comments hold up.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
  - Sceptic: tag changed from no to partly. Challenge: the audited reviewers compared new code with old code line by line, so "real differences" assumes a reference. Answer: accepted; checking the agent's replies to review comments still holds without one.
- **REV-9** [stated] Once agents write fast, waiting for approval becomes the bottleneck; plan reviewer capacity across the owning teams from the start.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2023–2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Google: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#who-did-what), [Spotify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#how-it-was-checked), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At Bloomberg reviewer time was not the whole limit: the moves were low priority and owners carried the deploy risk, so most PRs got no decision; its authors look to more checks inside the pipeline and to runs that owners request ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong)). At Asana, whose engineers reviewed their own agents' pull requests twice a day, slow lint and CI held the work up, not approval ([Asana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [verification not generation is the bottleneck](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2025-06-04-verification-not-generation-is-the-bottleneck.md), agrees.
- **REV-10** [ours] Grade a small sample of converted code against hand-converted versions with a rubric; pass rates say nothing about readability or idiom.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Strength: weak. Era: Claude 2.1, 2024.
  - Cases: [Slack: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Airbnb reports intent and coverage kept, with no quality grading ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#how-it-was-checked)).
- **REV-11** [stated] Code that meets the feature requirements can still duplicate logic, drift from the architecture or run slowly; keep reviewers who know the target platform.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026 (models unstated).
  - Cases: [Shopify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.

## Release and rollout (rollout.md)

How the new code reached users, and how risk was limited on the way.

- **ROL-1** [stated] Swap one component per change inside normal releases, old and new in one tree joined by a temporary bridge, so the main branch can always ship.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#practices-to-copy), [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Bun's author says doing everything at once beats an incremental move, and merged one branch after eleven days ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked)); Shopify chose a fresh native build over a gradual move inside the old app ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-was-migrated)) and released it whole after a beta ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#how-it-was-checked)).
- **ROL-2** [stated] Treat merged and released as separate gates: ship first to a canary or pre-release that few users take, and promote it only after real use.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Some GitHub regressions still reached a stable release ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked)).
- **ROL-3** [stated] Changes that reach many teams' systems still need slow production rollouts watched by their owners; the AI pipeline speeds the code, not this step.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: internal Gemini; Claude Sonnet 4.5, then Opus 4.6, 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: A downstream product took the whole Bun rewrite in one release and barely anyone noticed ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **ROL-4** [stated] Delete the old code in the same change that adds the new; concurrent edits to ported code then surface as rebase conflicts instead of silent losses.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Branch drift and rebases still caused a few regressions ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **ROL-5** [stated] Keep agent branches short-lived against a busy main branch; sessions left open for days pile up drift, and rebases lose changes.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **ROL-6** [ours] Track the size of the temporary bridge between old and new as the progress signal and drive it to zero; line counts on a busy code base mislead.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers).
  - Against: None found.
- **ROL-7** [stated] Ship a new failure boundary (such as hosting in-process) as an opt-in mode beside the old default, separate from the code port itself.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: weak. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: None found.
- **ROL-8** [stated] When old and new run side by side, send a unit that fails its tests back to the old framework rather than block the rollout or diagnose each failure.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Strength: weak. Era: unstated.
  - Cases: [Uber: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong), [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked).
  - Against: None found; Uber does not say how many units stayed on the old framework ([Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **ROL-9** [stated] Unrequested changes of low priority mostly sit undecided; let owners commit to the generated branch, and consider generating hard-to-check moves only when owners ask.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: Claude Sonnet 4.5, then Opus 4.6, 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; both remedies are plans the authors have not yet tried.

## Machines and operations (operations.md)

Running many agents on real machines, and keeping the result healthy after merge.

- **OPS-1** [stated] Parallel agents saturate CPU, disk and I/O: size the machine first, let one agent build at a time through a lease, and push full test runs to CI.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At Asana, CI results that differed from local checks, with a slow lint step, were where people had to step in most ([Asana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)): pushing runs to CI helps only if CI matches local runs.
- **OPS-2** [stated] Contain heavy tests with operating-system limits (control groups, process namespaces, disk quotas); asking the agent to be careful contains nothing.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Bun's limits covered memory, CPU and processes, yet the disk still filled and crashed the machine several times ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)); no case shows disk quotas in use.
- **OPS-3** [stated] Make the inner loop fast (module splits, build caches, host I/O) before scaling agents; their time goes mostly to reading, building and testing, not writing.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [Bun: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy), [Shopify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-went-wrong), [Asana: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At Shopify the slow step was not the build: hot reload did not help, because agents read and drove the app through simulators; its fix is a headless path into the app's logic ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-worked)).
- **OPS-4** [stated] List what the old runtime supplied silently (time zone, environment, process flags) and test every platform you ship; one green platform says little.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **OPS-5** [stated] Keep hardening after merge: repeated security review, round-the-clock fuzzing and leak tracking, with people reviewing the fixes they produce.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Disagree: the Zig creator says Bun was not fuzzing before the port, against the post's claim ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **OPS-6** [stated] Run bulk change jobs, by agent or by rule, as scheduled batches sized to the infrastructure, sort results into status groups, and rerun only what is stuck.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: strong. Era: 2023–2025.
  - Cases: [Slack: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Google: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-worked), [Airbnb: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked).
  - Against: At Bloomberg the job batches did not set the pace: PRs went out in a few bursts while merges came at a steady rate of their own ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Sceptic: tag changed from no to partly. Challenge: the status groups count how many converted old tests pass, so the old behaviour is the oracle. Answer: accepted; Google's groups count remaining sites instead, which needs no oracle.
- **OPS-7** [ours] Load-test the new code for blocking and resource exhaustion; one port froze its interface on a synchronous call across the bridge.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.

## Security (security.md)

Sandboxing agents, memory safety, dependencies and data integrity.

- **SEC-1** [stated] Run unattended agents in a minimal sandbox with an allowlist of commands; pushing, merging and talking to people belong to the surrounding infrastructure.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: Claude Code, 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: Bun's agents committed and pushed themselves and the project still finished ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [agent security is the wild west](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2025-06-16-agent-security-is-the-wild-west.md), agrees.
- **SEC-2** [stated] Whatever the harness exposes may get used unasked (an unlisted skill, git commands, a peer's worktree); remove what the task does not need.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Spotify itself is adding skills and self-gathered context because prompts grew unwieldy without them ([Spotify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **SEC-3** [ours] Block destructive repository and system commands in the tool layer, not with a prompt rule, which only arrives after the damage.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: None found.
- **SEC-4** [stated] After a port into a memory-safe language, count where unsafe code sits, allow it only at foreign and system boundaries, and have the compiler forbid it elsewhere.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Intel: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: Disagree: on how much to allow, Bun's faithful port keeps far more unsafe code and plans to cut it only by later refactoring ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **SEC-5** [stated] Generate foreign-function signatures with a binding tool and reject any model answer that differs; a wrong contract leaks unsafety into safe-looking code.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Intel: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-worked), [Intel: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: None found.
- **SEC-6** [ours] A bounds-checked target turns silent out-of-range access into crashes; expect new crash reports and test limits at real-world sizes.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **SEC-7** [ours] Treat each replaced library as a migration of its own, above all sanitizers, credential stores and protocol SDKs, and vet every new dependency.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; no case shows new dependencies being vetted.
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [rethink dependencies supply chain](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-03-24-rethink-dependencies-supply-chain.md), agrees.
  - Sceptic: tag changed from no to partly. Challenge: the library-swap regressions were caught as departures from the old behaviour. Answer: accepted; vetting new dependencies still holds without an old system.
- **SEC-8** [stated] Treat agent session logs and traces as data that may hold secrets; control where they are stored and where they are uploaded.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Spotify: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: None found.
- **SEC-9** [stated] Isolate each agent run from earlier attempts and reference answers, which it could otherwise read and lean on; decide about network access too.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Intel: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#who-did-what), [Bloomberg: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: None found.
- **SEC-10** [stated] Never let agents choose the order of schema changes, backfills or ownership of shared tables; one agent's chosen order would have lost data silently.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026 (models unstated).
  - Cases: [1Password: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong), [1Password: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: None found.

## Cost (cost.md)

Tokens, money, people's time and the bill after merge.

- **CST-1** [stated] Long agent runs are affordable only with high prompt-cache reuse: keep a stable prompt prefix and track the hit rate and each kind of token.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [Bun: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#numbers).
  - Against: With a model call per file, Zalando put its API bill under $40 per repository before any cache discount ([Zalando](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#numbers)); the cache matters most for long agent runs. Zalando still ordered its prompt for caching ([Zalando](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-worked)).
- **CST-2** [ours] Ask for the full bill: tokens at the price paid, people's hours by role, compute and CI, review, and the work after merge; most sources give one piece.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [Bun: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#numbers), [Airbnb: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: GitHub gives the fullest token breakdown in the set ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers)).
- **CST-3** [ours] Expect cost per unit to have a long tail; report median and mean, and size the budget for hub components and hard files.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2026.
  - Cases: [Intel: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [Airbnb: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **CST-4** [ours] Before reusing a published cost, check the model, how it was reached and the price basis; pre-release, internal or partner models give costs others cannot repeat.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: model-specific by definition.
  - Cases: [Bun: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#who-did-what), [Intel: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#who-did-what), [Google: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#who-did-what), [Asana: source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#source).
  - Against: None found.
- **CST-5** [ours] Work out cost per unit inside one case and name the unit; added lines, production lines, symbols and files differ, and tokens do not convert to money across cases.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#numbers), [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [Intel: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#numbers).
  - Against: None found.
- **CST-6** [ours] Count the work after merge (regression fixes, security rounds, fuzzing, clean-up and speed work) in what the migration cost.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **CST-7** [ours] Budget review agents as a multiple of generation (several reviewers and a fixer per writer), and ask for their share of tokens, which no case reports.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#who-did-what), [GitHub: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: None found.
- **CST-8** [stated] Missing or broken tests in target repositories shift the cost of checking onto the teams that receive the changes; the central figures leave it out.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2023–2026.
  - Cases: [Spotify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#how-it-was-checked), [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **CST-9** [ours] Pipeline and harness costs pay back over many repositories or migrations; a one-off project should reuse a general harness rather than build one.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Spotify: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#numbers), [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Airbnb built its own pipeline for one migration and finished far inside its manual estimate ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what)), and Slack's author expects custom pipelines to stay necessary ([Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)).

## Team and roles (team.md)

Who does what when agents write most of the code.

- **TEM-1** [stated] The lead engineer's job becomes running the control loop: framing slices, challenging design, pushing for completeness, deciding every merge.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [GitHub: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#who-did-what), [Bun: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: GitHub's split of the engineer's messages by intent was labelled by an LLM, not checked by a person ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [partial autonomy and autonomy slider](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2025-06-17-partial-autonomy-and-autonomy-slider.md), agrees.
- **TEM-2** [stated] Count the people behind a one-engineer story (reviewers in many teams, interop, packaging and build specialists) and staff and budget for them.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2023–2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#who-did-what), [Google: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#who-did-what), [Slack: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: Bun credits the port to one engineer and names no helpers for it ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#who-did-what)).
- **TEM-3** [stated] A central team should own the agent tooling, build it with early adopters, and teach prompt writing; untrained users fell into the same traps.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: Claude 2.1, 2024; Claude Code, 2025.
  - Cases: [Spotify: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#who-did-what), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Slack: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: None found.
- **TEM-4** [stated] Review in two tiers: the migration owner screens each batch, then code owners accept; expect the load to spread over many teams.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2023–2026.
  - Cases: [Google: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#how-it-was-checked), [Spotify: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#who-did-what), [Bloomberg: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: In Bun one engineer merged alone, with no second tier ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#who-did-what)).
- **TEM-5** [stated] Code the model migrates is code the team never wrote; keep owners close to it and teach them the new library, or reviews and debugging suffer.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: GPT-4o, 2024–2025.
  - Cases: [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.

## Rule-based tools and AI (tooling.md)

Splitting the work between deterministic tools and models.

- **TOL-1** [stated] Have agents build deterministic tools (analysers, call-site manifests, porting guides, ownership tables), review those, then bind later agent work to them.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked), [Bun: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked), [Intel: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: Ordering errors persisted at 1Password even with explicit rules in place ([1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **TOL-2** [stated] Run a rule-based codemod first and give the model its partial output, with a note wherever the rules gave up; it anchors the model.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: Claude 2.1, 2024; internal Gemini.
  - Cases: [Slack: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Google: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: Uber's recipes made all its rewrites with no model step, and its attempt to have AI migrate several files at once failed ([Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#who-did-what)).
  - Sceptic: tag changed from no to partly. Challenge: a codemod needs old code to transform, and its gain came together with rendered output captured by running the old tests. Answer: accepted.
- **TOL-3** [stated] Find change sites with a code index or static analysis, include too many rather than too few, and let the model edit the whole file around each hint.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: internal Gemini; 2026.
  - Cases: [Google: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-worked), [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked).
  - Against: The index can miss sites beyond its hop limit ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Sceptic: tag changed from no to partly. Challenge: including too many sites is safe only because regression suites and slow rollouts catch the misses. Answer: accepted.
- **TOL-4** [stated] Price the rule-based alternative with the upkeep of its rules; hand-written transforms keep growing on long-tail patterns, which is where models pay off.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2024–2025.
  - Cases: [Spotify: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#numbers), [Slack: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong), [Google: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-worked), [Zalando: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Uber kept writing recipes for each common build failure and sent failing files back to the old framework, so rules alone carried its long tail while a model attempt failed ([Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong)). At Slack the codemod's output still steered the model better than prompt work ([Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked)), so rules stay in the system.
- **TOL-5** [stated] Keep agents and models behind your own thin interface, log traces from day one, and pin model and settings per run; the best agent changed within a year.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2023–2026.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Google: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: Disagree: GitHub switched models per slice and mid-session, trading repeatability for fit ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [plan for intelligence brownouts](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-03-11-plan-for-intelligence-brownouts.md), agrees.
- **TOL-6** [stated] Set up linters, formatters, type checks and coding instructions before the first change, and run them inside the agent's loop, not only in CI.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy), [Airbnb: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Slack: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked).
  - Against: At Shopify, with guidance, linting, tests and static analysis in place, generated code could still repeat logic or drift from the architecture, so native experts stayed essential ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-went-wrong)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [agents ignore code style rules](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-03-21-agents-ignore-code-style-rules.md), agrees.
- **TOL-7** [stated] Before choosing a model for a mechanical framework move, try deterministic rewrites on a typed syntax tree; at very large scale they were judged more practical.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: weak. Era: unstated.
