  - Cases: [Uber: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong), [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Slack's codemod alone left work that a model then finished ([Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked)); Airbnb's LLM pipeline moved a test framework with no rule-based core ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked)).
- **TOL-8** [stated] Give agents a direct way to inspect and drive the running app (state, events, commands, logic run headless); screenshots and accessibility trees made each test take minutes.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026 (models unstated).
  - Cases: [Shopify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-went-wrong), [Shopify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-worked).
  - Against: None found; Shopify gives no measured result for its headless CLI ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-worked)).
- **TOL-9** [stated] Where the old format is regular, have the model fill a schema-checked data object and let templates write the new files; one template fix then repairs every target.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: Claude Sonnet 4.5, 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked), [Bloomberg: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: The extraction path still produced a PR for only part of the tasks in each archetype, with reasons not given ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **TOL-10** [stated] At each model upgrade, review the pre-processing built to cover the older model's gaps; keep a step only if it adds reproducibility or eases debugging.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: Claude Sonnet 4.5, then Opus 4.6, 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: The same authors warn that handing too much to the model makes a pipeline fragile when model behaviour shifts between versions ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong)).

## Context and prompts (context.md)

What goes into the model's context, and how prompts are written.

- **CTX-1** [stated] Choosing the right context (nearby files, good examples, runtime data, exact mapping tables) moved results more than polishing the prompt wording.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: strong. Era: 2023–2026.
  - Cases: [Airbnb: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Slack: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Zalando: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-worked), [Asana: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Spotify treats prompt writing as the hard skill users lack ([Spotify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong)). Zalando credits a system prompt and clearer wording as well as mappings and examples ([Zalando](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-worked)).
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [context engineering](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2025-06-25-context-engineering.md), agrees.
- **CTX-2** [stated] Give the model the runtime facts a person would look at, such as the rendered output of each test, not only the source file.
  - Old system as oracle: yes. Strength: medium. Era: Claude 2.1, 2024.
  - Cases: [Slack: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Slack: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#practices-to-copy), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong), [Shopify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-worked).
  - Against: None found.
- **CTX-3** [stated] Write field and API mappings as explicit tables in the context, not prose; a guide adapted from the human one led to wrong mappings.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: GPT-4o, 2024; Claude Code, 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At Asana a much longer written guide to the target's conventions made results worse, and the code base's own examples sufficed ([Asana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)); that guide was prose, as the lesson warns, but more text was not better.
- **CTX-4** [stated] State the whole end state, its preconditions and when not to act; agents read vague goals narrowly and leave parts of the work out of scope.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy), [1Password: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#practices-to-copy), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At 1Password the same ordering mistakes came back after the agents were told explicitly about order and constraints ([1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong)): a clear statement is not enough on its own.
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [success criteria not steps](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-01-26-success-criteria-not-steps.md), agrees.
- **CTX-5** [stated] Put one change in each prompt; prompts bundling several changes ran out of context or stopped halfway.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: Claude Code, 2025.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: Zalando put about three components in each prompt and held accuracy by capping the prompt's size instead ([Zalando](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#numbers), [grouping](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-worked)); the limit may be context size, not the number of changes.
- **CTX-6** [stated] Prefer large, static, version-controlled prompts and few tools for predictability; letting the agent fetch context through many tools adds variance.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: Claude Code, 2025.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Spotify is now letting its agent gather context itself ([Spotify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong)), and GitHub ran broad tool sets and finished ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked)).
- **CTX-7** [stated] Ask the agent after each session what its prompt lacked, and fold the answer into the next version of the prompt.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: Claude Code, 2025.
  - Cases: [Spotify: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: None found.
- **CTX-8** [stated] Fit the prompt to the agent: a weak home-built loop needed step-by-step lists, while a stronger agent did better with the end state and room to plan.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: Claude Code against a home-built loop, 2025; Codex, 2026.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-worked), [Asana: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Asana: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found; 1Password's templates and playbook show step detail still helps on bounded edits ([1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked)).
- **CTX-9** [stated] When the context budget is small, choose context by fixed rules: full bodies of nearby functions, signatures for the rest, the hardest callers first.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Intel: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: Airbnb, with a large context budget, filled prompts with dozens of related files, also chosen by rules ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked)); the lesson is for small budgets.
- **CTX-10** [stated] Agents learn from the repository as it stands: fix docs and agent guidance that still favour the old library, and awkward examples, or they spread.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: Codex, 2026.
  - Cases: [Asana: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.

## Many agents at once (orchestration.md)

Running several agents in parallel without them wrecking each other.

- **ORC-1** [stated] Agents sharing one working copy wreck each other's work; give each writer its own worktree, or restrict git to committing its own files.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [1Password: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-worked), [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [Shopify: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#what-worked).
  - Against: One worktree per agent would have filled Bun's disk, so it used a few shared ones with git restricted ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **ORC-2** [stated] Run agents in parallel only on changes that are independent by design; otherwise parallelism adds inconsistency.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [1Password: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#practices-to-copy), [Asana: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: None found.
- **ORC-3** [stated] Peer agents on adjacent code need a named coordinator or human tiebreaker, and autonomy must stop at anything outside the agent's own branch.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026 (GPT-5.6 Sol, Opus 4.8 sessions).
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#practices-to-copy).
  - Against: The GitHub author blames splitting the work from both ends so that they met at the hub, not missing coordination ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong)); a coordinator patches a split that is better avoided.
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [delegate long tasks decompose well](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-02-25-delegate-long-tasks-decompose-well.md), agrees.
- **ORC-4** [stated] Build the work queue from deterministic output (compiler errors by module, failing traces per command), run the tool once, then fan the items out.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked), [Airbnb: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: GitHub's agents recompiled after each small edit and the author credits that loop ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked)); Bun's run-once queue also followed from banning builds in shared checkouts ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **ORC-5** [stated] Within one workspace, fan reading out to subagents and keep the edits with one agent; reading far outnumbered editing.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers).
  - Against: Parallel writing still worked with a separate workspace per writer: GitHub's child sessions ported in their own worktrees ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked)), and Bun ran dozens of writers split by crate ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked)).
  - Sceptic: tag kept at no. Challenge: the reading-to-editing ratio was measured in a port, where much reading was of the old code. Answer: kept at "no": reading old code is input, not an oracle; the ratio may differ in new work, which the Era and Strength already limit.
- **ORC-6** [stated] Prefer a short leash to a complex multi-agent design where you can: fixed code picks context, order and output place, and the model translates one unit.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Intel: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-worked), [Intel: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#practices-to-copy), [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Disagree: Bun and GitHub ran fleets of dozens of agents and finished ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked)) ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked)), and Shopify split its Shop port across specialised subagents ([Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#who-did-what)). Asana backs only the first half: a few agents with a loose goal finished, while sub-agents and tracked tickets did worse ([Asana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)).

## Agent failure modes (agent-failures.md)

How agents went wrong, so a plan can expect it.

- **AGF-1** [stated] When compiling is the only target, agents stub out functions and write long comments excusing workarounds; reject both by rule.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Intel: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Intel says catching stubs without per-function tests is still unsolved ([Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)), so the rule needs a check that can find them.
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [agents ignore code style rules](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-03-21-agents-ignore-code-style-rules.md), agrees.
- **AGF-2** [stated] Agents fill gaps in the spec with plausible guesses and carry them through many edits; make them check formats and ownership against code or data, or stop and ask.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [1Password: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At 1Password the same mistakes returned after agents were told the rules explicitly ([1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong)); telling agents to check is not enough without a tool or a person enforcing it.
  - Related view (karpathy-ideas): [coding agents make subtle conceptual mistakes](https://github.com/ntroccoli/karpathy-ideas/blob/main/ideas/2026-01-26-coding-agents-make-subtle-conceptual-mistakes.md), agrees.
- **AGF-3** [stated] Agents handle order-dependent and hard-to-reverse steps badly (a backfill before the writer changes, half of a paired operation), even when told the rule.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [1Password: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **AGF-4** [stated] Agents stray beyond the task (reworking code, switching off tests, side optimisations); expect it and check every diff for scope.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: internal Gemini to 2026.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: At GitHub agents also read vague prompts too narrowly and left work out ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong)), and the lead engineer, not only the agents, sometimes broke the translate-first rule; check scope in both directions.
- **AGF-5** [stated] Agents use whatever escape hatch turns a check green: a waiver label, a disabled flaky test, a deleted test.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **AGF-6** [ours] Make each agent session discardable as a unit; one unchecked assumption forced a whole session to be rolled back.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [1Password: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **AGF-7** [stated] Output varies between runs on the same input: plan retries, pick among passing attempts, and contain the variance in production migrations.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: internal Gemini to 2026.
  - Cases: [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong), [1Password: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Zalando: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#what-went-wrong), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
  - Sceptic: tag changed from no to partly. Challenge: picking among passing attempts needs something to pass, and here that was the old regression suite. Answer: accepted; any oracle will do, but one is needed.
- **AGF-8** [stated] Check how well the model handles each language in scope; one poorly supported language fell back to people.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: internal Gemini; likely era-bound.
  - Cases: [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.

## Human oversight (oversight.md)

Where people stay in the loop, and what they guard.

- **OVS-1** [stated] The agent that changes the code must not change what counts as correct: edits to tests, snapshots, baselines and waiver labels need a separate owner's approval.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#practices-to-copy), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Bun: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Intel: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **OVS-2** [stated] Keep the final merge with a person who checks how the agent answered CI and review, not only the diff.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#how-it-was-checked), [Google: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#how-it-was-checked), [Slack: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what), [Shopify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Disagree: in Bun no person read every line; the engineer checked the reviewers instead ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#how-it-was-checked)), and an outside critic calls it unreviewed.
- **OVS-3** [stated] Decide up front where automation stops (a retry cap, a residue size, a category for people) and hand over with the failed attempt as the starting point.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2023–2026.
  - Cases: [Airbnb: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Airbnb: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#practices-to-copy), [1Password: practices to copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#practices-to-copy), [Google: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#who-did-what), [Bloomberg: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#who-did-what), [Bloomberg: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Uber's stop rule was a revert to the old framework, not a hand-over to people ([Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **OVS-4** [stated] Bind each human approval to the exact text approved, such as a hash of the plan, so an agent's later edit to the plan needs a fresh approval.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: weak. Era: 2025–2026 (models unstated).
  - Cases: [Shopify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: None found.

## Knowledge capture (knowledge.md)

Turning failures and logs into lasting improvements.

- **KNW-1** [stated] When a failure recurs, fix what generates the code (prompt, reviewer rule, skill, evaluation, harness), not only the output; the second time is the trigger.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: 2024–2026.
  - Cases: [Bun: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-worked), [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked), [Airbnb: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked), [Zalando: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#how-it-was-checked), [Shopify: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md#how-it-was-checked), [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked).
  - Against: None found.
- **KNW-2** [stated] Stamp each unit with its status, tune against the largest failing group using a small sample, then sweep all units again.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: strong. Era: 2023–2025.
  - Cases: [Airbnb: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Slack: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-worked), [Google: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-worked), [Uber: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-worked).
  - Against: None found.
- **KNW-3** [stated] Keep structured session logs from the start; they later answered where time went and what people did, and became evaluations.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers), [GitHub: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-worked).
  - Against: GitHub's split of the engineer's messages by intent was labelled by an LLM, not checked by a person ([GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#numbers)).

## Measuring and reading results (measurement.md)

How to read the numbers in these sources, and how to report your own.

- **MSR-1** [ours] Treat savings measured against a manual effort that never ran as self-estimates; record the basis beside each figure and never add them across cases.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: all.
  - Cases: [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong), [Spotify: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#numbers), [Airbnb: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#numbers), [Slack: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#numbers), [Bun: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#numbers), [1Password: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Google's estimate at least agrees with its measured shares of model-made edits ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#numbers)).
- **MSR-2** [ours] For every success rate ask out of what (attempted, opened, merged, dropped from scope), and report each measure with its base; bases differed several-fold.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: all.
  - Cases: [Spotify: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#what-went-wrong), [Slack: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#how-it-was-checked), [Zalando: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md#how-it-was-checked), [Bloomberg: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#how-it-was-checked).
  - Against: Airbnb's main rate covers its whole file set ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#numbers)).
- **MSR-3** [ours] Weigh each source by the author's stake in the tool (seller, owner, partner); none of the cases had outside measurement.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: all.
  - Cases: [Bun: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#who-did-what), [GitHub: context](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#context), [Spotify: context](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#context), [1Password: context](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#context), [Intel: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: Google lists its own threats to validity ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong)), and Slack has no stake in the model it used ([Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what)).
- **MSR-4** [stated] Credit a gain to the migration only after separating it from work that landed in the same window (other speed work, linker changes, unrelated fixes).
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Disagree: the Zig creator credits link-time optimisation the old toolchain already had for Bun's speed-up ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **MSR-5** [stated] Escaped defects are unknown by nature: publish known regressions as a floor, grouped by cause, and use a before-and-after proxy labelled as a proxy.
  - Old system as oracle: partly. Strength: medium. Era: 2026.
  - Cases: [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong), [Bun: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Airbnb reports no defects after merge at all, which is missing data, not evidence ([Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **MSR-6** [ours] Activity numbers (lines per minute, commits, merged changes) are not progress; track verified behaviour or the shrinking list of remaining sites.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: all.
  - Cases: [Bun: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#numbers), [Spotify: numbers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#numbers), [GitHub: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: None found.
- **MSR-7** [ours] Re-date a lesson before reusing it: early negative results, and results from pre-release or restricted models, may not hold for the models you use.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: Claude 2.1 (2024) to pre-release models (2026).
  - Cases: [Slack: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what), [Bun: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#who-did-what), [Intel: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md#who-did-what), [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong), [Uber: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: 1Password's 2026 agents still broke ordering rules ([1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#what-went-wrong)), so some failures persist across eras.
- **MSR-8** [ours] Do not credit the model with work the deterministic tools did: finding sites, building manifests and codemods were often the hard part.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: strong. Era: all.
  - Cases: [Google: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#who-did-what), [Slack: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md#who-did-what), [1Password: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md#who-did-what), [Spotify: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md#who-did-what), [Uber: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md#who-did-what), [Bloomberg: who did what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#who-did-what).
  - Against: In Bun almost all the work ran through agent workflows ([Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md#who-did-what)).
- **MSR-9** [stated] If you will claim savings, measure people's share from file snapshots or logs from day one; estimates from the tool's own builders are biased.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: internal Gemini.
  - Cases: [Google: how it was checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#how-it-was-checked), [Google: what went wrong](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong).
  - Against: Google itself warns that edit distance misses the thinking behind edits, and the snapshot method skips edits made along the way, so it understates people's share ([Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md#what-went-wrong)).
- **MSR-10** [stated] A merge rate undercounts unrequested changes: also count targets whose owners rejected the change and then migrated anyway, often reusing it.
  - Old system as oracle: no. Strength: medium. Era: Claude Sonnet 4.5, then Opus 4.6, 2025–2026.
  - Cases: [Bloomberg: what worked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked).
  - Against: Bloomberg followed up only the rejected Python PRs, not the far larger group left without a decision ([Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md#what-worked)).

## Cases

- [Bloomberg opens 2,333 migration PRs for Python packaging and C++ builds with a hybrid pipeline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md) — mixed, an in-house shared-environment Python packaging model; CppBuild, an in-house C++ build system to PyPackaging, an in-house per-package dependency model; CMake; AI share: part; evidence: shown-in-source; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. A rule-driven pipeline with Claude in bounded steps opened 2,333 packaging and build PRs; 729 were merged, and most got no decision from their owners.
- [GitHub moves its Copilot agent runtime from TypeScript to Rust using agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md) — language, TypeScript on Node.js and V8 to Rust (native library with a C ABI); AI share: most; evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$120,000 for ~136.3 billion tokens (engineer time not priced). One engineer steered agent fleets to port about 430,000 lines of TypeScript to Rust in place, one component per PR, over 14.5 weeks.
- [Shopify rebuilds its React Native mobile apps natively for iOS and Android](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md) — language, React Native apps (Shop first; Shopify, Point of Sale, Inbox to follow) to native iOS (Swift, SwiftUI) and Android (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose) apps; AI share: unstated; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Agents port Shopify's React Native apps to native iOS and Android code through gated checkpoints; one-shot ports failed, and the Shop app shipped in 12 weeks.
- [Intel's IDEAS harness ports the libgit2 command-line client in C to safe Rust](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md) — language, C (libgit2 command-line client) to safe Rust (no unsafe code); AI share: most; evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$0.55 per symbol for translation (total unstated), plus ~$6.5 for repair. An LLM harness turned 112K lines of C into safe Rust that compiled but crashed; 8 person-hours guiding an agent got git blame working.
- [Asana finishes its Enzyme to React Testing Library move with Codex agents in two weeks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md) — test-framework, Enzyme (frontend React tests) to React Testing Library; AI share: unstated; evidence: assertion-only; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$11,000 model usage plus ~$1,000 infrastructure. Up to 4 Codex agents on a 5-sentence prompt removed Enzyme in about 1.5 weeks of engineering time for about $12K; stale docs and slow lint got in the way.
- [Bun moves its JavaScript runtime off Zig onto Rust with Claude agents in 11 days](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md) — language, Zig (Bun runtime, bundler, package manager, test runner) to Rust (about 100 crates); AI share: most; evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: ~$165,000 at API list prices for the tokens used before merge (690 million output tokens, 5.9 billion fresh input tokens, 72 billion cached input tokens). One engineer ran about 50 Claude Code workflows, up to 64 agents at once, to port 535K lines of Zig to Rust in 11 days; 19 known regressions, all fixed.
- [1Password uses AI agents to refactor its Go monolith and begin a service extraction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md) — architecture, Go monolith (B5), database transactions opened with MustBegin (panics on failure) to separately owned services; transaction calls that return errors; AI share: unstated; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Agents rewrote over 3,000 panicking transaction calls from a tight spec, but stumbled on a service extraction's ordering and invariants.
- [Uber moves 75K test classes off JUnit 4 onto JUnit 5 with OpenRewrite; an AI attempt failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md) — test-framework, Java tests on JUnit 4 in a Bazel monorepo to Java tests on JUnit 5 (Jupiter engine on the JUnit Platform); AI share: little; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Contrast case. Rule-based OpenRewrite recipes moved over 75,000 Java test classes onto JUnit 5; a generative-AI attempt failed and AI only helped debug.
- [Spotify runs fleet-wide migrations with its Honk background coding agent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md) — mixed, many (for example Java AutoValue classes, old Scio versions, deprecated datasets) to many (for example Java records, the newest Scio, new dataset versions); AI share: most; evidence: assertion-only; author: seller-of-tool; cost: unstated. Spotify put a coding agent inside its fleet migration tooling; verifiers and an LLM judge gate each PR, and over 1,500 agent PRs were merged.
- [Google widens int32 IDs to int64 in 39 migrations with an LLM pipeline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md) — data, int32 ID fields in protocol buffer schemas and the code using them (Java, C++, Dart and others) to int64 ID fields; AI share: most; evidence: shown-in-source; author: seller-of-tool; cost: unstated. A nightly pipeline of code search, rule-based sorting, an internal Gemini model and staged checks drafted 74.45% of 595 code changes in 39 ID migrations.
- [Airbnb moves 3.5K React test files off Enzyme onto React Testing Library](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md) — test-framework, Enzyme (React component tests) to React Testing Library; AI share: most; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. An LLM pipeline with per-file validation steps and retries migrated 97% of about 3,500 React test files; people finished the rest by hand.
- [Zalando moves partner apps from one in-house UI component library to another with GPT-4o](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md) — framework, in-house UI component library (React) to another in-house UI component library (React); AI share: part; evidence: assertion-only; author: user-of-tool; cost: under $40 per repository in GPT-4o API fees (estimate). A Python tool fed GPT-4o hand-checked mappings and examples per component group; about 90% of migrated lines were right, and one bad change reached production.
- [Slack pairs a syntax-tree codemod with Claude 2.1 to help move 15K Enzyme tests to React Testing Library](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md) — test-framework, Enzyme (React unit and integration tests) to React Testing Library; AI share: unstated; evidence: shown-in-source; author: user-of-tool; cost: unstated. Codemod alone 45% (evaluation files), Claude 2.1 alone 40-60% (base not given), both 80% of code in 9 checked files; 22% of tests passed over 338 files.

## Before you migrate: checklist

Questions to answer about a repository before an AI-driven migration to another language,
framework or library, or a large restructuring. Each has a **Check** an agent runs on the
repository, an **Evidence** line saying in our words what the cases show ("ours" marks our own
inference), and the **Lessons** behind it (`TST-2` is lesson 2 on the testing page; pages are
listed in [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/llms.txt)).
Pitfalls by kind of move: [pitfalls.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/pitfalls.md).

Cases: [GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md) (TypeScript), [Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md) (Zig) and [Intel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-24-intel-ideas-c-to-rust.md) (C) to Rust; [1Password](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-20-1password-monolith-refactor.md) (Go
restructuring); [Spotify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md) and [Bloomberg](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-11-03-bloomberg-python-cpp-uplift.md) (fleet changes); [Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md), [Slack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2024-05-22-slack-enzyme-to-rtl.md) and [Asana](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-08-07-asana-enzyme-to-rtl.md)
(React tests); [Zalando](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-02-20-zalando-ui-component-libraries.md) (UI library); [Shopify](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-10-shopify-react-native-to-native.md) (React Native to native); [Google](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md) (wider
IDs); [Uber](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md) (Java tests, rule-based: a contrast case).

1. **Is the move allowed, possible and worth it?**
   Check: find the written reason and the measured problem behind it; repository rules that pin the stack, forbid new libraries or name an approver (one
   that forbids the target is a blocker); for each framework the product rests on (renderer, UI,
   desktop shell, platform or store SDK), its mature equivalent in the target, or mark the move a
   rewrite on a new base; where time, memory or money goes today (a profile, a bill) and whether
   the code to port is on that path; who maintains the result and whether they read the target
   language; what the target must win, as numbers where possible.
   Evidence: the cases start from a known problem or a forced move: GitHub's embedding, startup
   and memory, Bun's crashes and leaks, Slack's test library blocking a React upgrade, Google's
   IDs nearing the int32 limit. The rest is ours.
   Lessons: PLN-7, PLN-8, PLN-9, SEC-7.
2. **Is there a test oracle that survives the move and that the agent cannot edit?**
   Check: count the tests that exercise behaviour through a public interface (CLI, API, files
   written, a headless harness) apart from white-box tests; list public features with none; run
   them once and list those that fail or do not run. Find golden files tied to the old
   implementation and how they are regenerated. Say how results are compared across languages
   (plain-data summaries, tolerances) and how you confirm the tests ran. When the tests are what
   moves, say how intent and coverage are compared (coverage before and after, a hand-converted
   sample) and check new tests can fail. Say whether old and new can take the same inputs side by
   side and have their outputs compared (a differential or shadow run), and how late a wrong
   change first fails (build, tests, or only once deployed). Find who must approve a test change
   (CODEOWNERS, branch rules, CI, the owner); none is a finding.
   Evidence: GitHub's unchanged end-to-end suites were the oracle; its feature-loss regressions
   came almost all from their gaps. Bun's suite, in a third language, judged the
   whole port; a critic notes it had missed the old bugs. Google's correct changes stalled on
   failing tests and goldens;
   Spotify's worst case is green CI with wrong behaviour. Intel matched the C original's
   `git blame` output; Shopify compared both apps' screens and events at named points.
   Bloomberg's Python changes could fail only once deployed.
   Lessons: TST-1, TST-2, TST-3, TST-4, TST-5, TST-6, TST-8, TST-10, TST-12, VER-5, VER-11, OVS-1.
3. **Can an agent build, check and test alone, fast, and in parallel, in both toolchains?**
   Check: find the command that builds, formats, lints and tests one unit in the old stack, and
   name the one for the target stack (pin its toolchain). Use recorded timings first (logs, CI
   history); otherwise time each, count the output lines of a failure, and build two separate
   clones outside the repository at once. For the number
   of agents you plan, estimate compile time, disk space, disk speed and process limits; say how
   agents are kept from undoing each other's work, and which target platforms their machines can
   build and test; for an app, how an agent drives it and how long one test takes. A missing
   formatter or linter is a finding.
   Evidence: GitHub needed a build lock once many agents built at once. Bun's agents sharing one
   checkout undid each other's work within minutes, and heavy tests stalled the machine.
   1Password gave each agent a worktree; Spotify's verify tool returns short errors. Shopify's
   agents took minutes per test in simulators; Asana's people stepped in most over slow lint
   and CI that disagreed with local runs.
   Lessons: OPS-1, OPS-2, OPS-3, ORC-1, ORC-2, VER-2, VER-4, TOL-6, TOL-8.
4. **How big is the job, really?**
   Check: scope is everything that must exist in the target. Count lines and files in scope
   (`scc`, `tokei` or `cloc`, by folder) for
   code (GPU too), tests, build scripts, and other languages (shaders, generated files,
   templates or DSLs of the old stack). For a change across call sites, list every site with a
   code index or static analyzer, not text search alone, and keep the list. Add code tangled with
   the scope. List the data and asset formats both builds read, and stored data that must stay
   readable (rows, hashes, saves). Give the change rate in scope over the last quarter
   (`git log --since="3 months ago" --numstat --format=%ad --date=short -- <scope>`): commits and
   lines per week, active days, last change. Code still changing fast: ask the owner whether to
   wait, or delete the old code in the change that ports it so later edits conflict.
   Evidence: GitHub's scope grew about threefold as code moved in and colleagues kept adding to
   the old code. Google's code index beat text search
   but listed irrelevant sites; 1Password's analyzer listed every site.
   Lessons: PLN-3, PLN-10, ROL-4, TOL-1, TOL-3, MSR-8.
5. **Can the work ship in small units, with old and new side by side?**
   Check: split the scope into units (files, components, packages, repositories), draw their
   dependency order with a read-only graph tool for the language (`go mod graph`, `cargo tree`,
   `jdeps`, `madge`, `pydeps`), and count the cycles (Go and Cargo forbid package cycles: look
   between modules or files instead), and mark the leaves that touch neither I/O nor shared
   state. Find the seam that lets one unit switch while the rest stays, and how the build links
   both languages meanwhile (seams by kind of move: [pitfalls.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/pitfalls.md#seams)). No seam:
   say so, the move is one switch. Check what the platform rules allow. Pick the pilot units.
   Evidence: GitHub swapped one component per pull request through a temporary interop layer,
   leaves first; Intel went in dependency order; Google, Airbnb and Spotify moved one ID, file or
   repository at a time. Bun made one switch after a small trial, and cycles left by its package
   split took two more agent runs. Shopify's one-pass port of a whole app gave code it could not
   ship; small reviewed checkpoints replaced it. The cost of a mixed build is ours.
   Lessons: PLN-1, PLN-4, PLN-11, ROL-1, ROL-6, ORC-4.
6. **Is the end state written, and is the scope held?**
   Check: look for a written target for the whole migration (not one unit), before-and-after
   examples from this repository, sites grouped into patterns with a template each, when the
   agent must stop and escalate, a rule to translate first and redesign later, and a check on
   each diff for changes outside its scope. A repository rule against translating first (delete
   old paths, keep no compatibility) is a finding.
   Evidence: GitHub's agents ported only the hot paths until the full end state was written, and
   each redesign the lead allowed during the port cost regressions, time or tokens. Bun wrote a
   porting guide first and left idiomatic code for later. 1Password's call-site cleanup ran from
   a list, templates and escalation rules; Spotify's judge rejects sessions mostly for straying
   from the prompt.
   Lessons: CTX-4, PLN-2, PLN-5, REV-4, AGF-2, AGF-4.
7. **What does the old stack do implicitly?**
   Check: search the scope for behaviour the target will not give for free, starting from the
   lists for this kind of move in [pitfalls.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/pitfalls.md); mark each item "like for like" or
   "needs a decision" and give the search you used. Make a
   table of direct dependencies: target library, version, stable release or archived (a missing
   framework is question 1).
   Evidence: the regressions compiled: GitHub's runtime defaults and one-sided paired operations,
   Bun's lines that read alike but behave differently, Intel's pointer comparison, Google's bit
   operations and SQL tied to the old width, 1Password's backfill order, Zalando's layouts that
   broke once deployed.
   Lessons: REV-3, OPS-4, TST-7, VER-6, SEC-5, SEC-6, AGF-3, SEC-10.
8. **Is the code uniform enough for one prompt, and what context goes with it?**
   Check: group the units by kind of code (pure logic, concurrency, OS layer, GPU or UI, data
   pipelines) and by framework, build system and style. For each group, name the context an
   agent gets: the unit's source, its neighbours' tests, good examples, mapping tables for
   renamed fields or APIs, runtime facts a person would look at, and what a rule-based codemod
   can do first. Pilot the model on the hardest files of each language in scope, and check the
   largest files fit its context window. A group too varied for one prompt is a candidate to defer
   or do by hand. Search docs and agent instructions for advice favouring the old stack.
   Evidence: Spotify dropped a framework too varied for one prompt, and mapping tables fixed
   wrong field mappings; Airbnb found the choice of related files mattered more than prompt
   wording; Slack gave the model a codemod's partial output and each test's rendered output;
   Google's model handled Dart poorly, so people did it. Uber's recipes did a test-framework move
   where its AI attempt failed. Bloomberg gave each archetype its own prompt and checks; stale
   docs misled Asana's agents.
   Lessons: CTX-1, CTX-2, CTX-3, CTX-5, CTX-9, CTX-10, TOL-2, TOL-7, TOL-9, AGF-8, PLN-8, PLN-12.
9. **How will you work the long tail, stop, and learn from failures?**
   Check: look for a status record per unit, a way to rerun failing units by step, a retry limit
   (for independent units such as files; where units depend on each other, a rule to fix the
   workflow and rerun instead), a rule for when to stop automating and finish by hand, and a place
   where a failure seen twice becomes a standing instruction, skill or eval.
   Evidence: Airbnb stamped each file with its status, swept again after each fix and finished
   the last files by hand; Intel capped retries. Bun fixed the process, not
   the code, when agents stubbed functions; GitHub turned repeated failures into instructions,
   skills and evals; Spotify asks the agent what its prompt lacked; Zalando reran a golden set
   after each prompt change. Uber put files whose tests failed back on the old framework.
   Lessons: VER-3, KNW-1, KNW-2, OVS-3, CTX-7, AGF-7, OPS-6, ROL-8, TST-11.
10. **What may the agent decide and reach alone, and who reviews?**
    Check: list the guardrails an agent could switch off (deleting or editing tests, updating
    snapshots or baselines, waiver labels, CI flags) and who must approve each; the steps kept
    for people (schema changes, backfills, deploy order); and the tools, skills and credentials
    agent sessions can reach. A rule written only in a document, with nothing enforcing it, is a
    partial gap. Ask the owner who reviews, whether they read the target language, and how many
    hours a week they have.
    Evidence: a GitHub agent applied a waiver label to pass a failing check, and a session merged
    a peer's worktree unasked; Spotify's agents switched off unreliable tests; Bun's agents
    stubbed functions until reviewer agents, seeing only the diff, rejected that; 1Password's
    agents repeated ordering mistakes after being told. Bloomberg's owners left most unrequested
    PRs undecided; Shopify needed reviewers who knew the target platform.
    Lessons: OVS-1, OVS-2, AGF-1, AGF-5, SEC-1, SEC-2, SEC-3, REV-1, REV-2, REV-9, REV-11, TEM-4,
    ROL-9.
11. **How will changes reach users?**
    Check: find the release channels (pre-release, flags, canary), the share of users each
    reaches, how problems are reported and watched, and how one unit's change is rolled back (for
    a single-user or internal tool: what a release and a rollback are). Not released yet: mark it
    "not applicable yet" and say what must exist before the first release.
    Evidence: GitHub aimed to ship each port to a pre-release first, yet some regressions reached
    a stable release; Bun's merged build stayed a canary while regressions were fixed; Google
    rolled its largest migrations out slowly, owners watching. A rollback path per unit is ours.
    Lessons: ROL-2, ROL-3, ROL-5, ROL-7, VER-1, OPS-5.
12. **How will you measure cost and result?**
    Check: write down the manual estimate and how it was made. Measure, before the port and on
    fixed hardware, the number the product exists for (speed, latency, memory, output quality),
    and the part the port changes, if not the same path. Plan to record tokens or spend, engineer
    hours, pull requests, regressions after merge and reverts, marking measured against estimated.
    Evidence: GitHub benchmarked before and after (other changes landed in the same window) and
    gave its token bill; Bun priced its tokens at list rates and counted regressions
    after merge; Google measured shares as edit distance. Every manual-effort or saving figure is
    the team's own estimate. Bloomberg also counted undecided PRs, and owners' migrations that
    reused rejected ones. Recording reverts is ours.
    Lessons: CST-1, CST-2, CST-6, CST-7, MSR-1, MSR-2, MSR-4, MSR-5, MSR-9, MSR-10, TST-9, KNW-3.

### Starting thresholds

Only where a case gives a number: starting points from one case each, not targets. Elsewhere,
judge "gap" from the Check alone.

- Q4: GitHub's first count was about 130,000 lines and about 430,000 went through the port. A
  scope count with no allowance for inflow is a partial gap.
  [GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-09-16-github-copilot-runtime-rust.md)
- Q5: Bun ran its whole loop on 3 files before all 1,448. No pilot before the bulk run is a gap.
  [Bun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-07-08-bun-zig-to-rust.md)
- Q9: most of Airbnb's simple and medium files passed within about 10 attempts; 50 to 100
  attempts on the hardest gained little. It tuned each fix on 5 to 10 failing files. No retry
  limit, or no rule to stop and hand-port, is a gap. [Airbnb](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md)

### How to run this checklist

1. Run it in a fresh session on the repository to migrate, changing nothing there. The cases are
   few and mostly teams' own accounts: read their "What went wrong" sections before relying on them.
2. Measure first: answer each Check with a number, file or command output, not from memory.
3. A check you may not run: write the exact command, mark it "not run" with the reason, never guess its result. Logs or CI history
   count if you say where they came from.
4. A fact only the owner knows (review time, budget, approval of a new stack): write the question
   and mark it "ask the owner".
5. Mark each question "gap", "partial gap", "no gap" or "not applicable yet", with the
   measurement.
6. Write proposals from the Evidence lines and, if you can open them, the cited lessons (their
   "Against" lines and oracle tags) and the case sections they link, above all "Practices to
   copy". Compare numbers across cases only when their units match.
7. Order proposals by what blocks the rest: blockers first (a "no" on question 1 is the usual
   one), then what others depend on (the oracle, the baseline, the end state), then the rest.
   After a no-go on question 1, give the verdict and the blockers, and list the other gaps one
   line each, with no proposals.
8. Report as below and wait for the owner's choice.
9. Record: once the owner has chosen, write `docs/migration-review.md` in the measured repository
   (the one file this checklist adds there): each proposal with its status and, for proven and
   stopped holding, the event that shows it and its date. In a read-only run, put the record
   after the report instead.
10. Revisit: a later run reads that record first and re-checks only the open, waiting and
    stopped-holding items, plus any question whose measurement may have moved. Update each status with the date and the event; reopen proven or skipped
    items only if their check now fails.

### Report format

```markdown
# Before-you-migrate review: <repository>, <YYYY-MM-DD>

Migration: <from> to <to>. Scope measured: <lines and files by kind, units, change rate>.
Go / no-go: go | go after the blockers | no-go — <one line why>.

## Blockers
- Q<n>: <what must happen first, and who decides>.

## Not run
- Q<n>: `<exact command>` — <why it was not run>.

## Ask the owner
- Q<n>: <question>.

## No gap
- Q<n> <question>: <measurement>.

## Not applicable yet
- Q<n> <question>: <why, and what must exist first>.

## Proposals

1. Q<n> <question> — gap | partial gap.
   Today: <what the repository does, with the measurement>.
   Change: <the proposal>.
   Evidence: Q<n>, its lesson IDs, and links to case sections you read.
   Depends on: <proposal numbers, or none>.
   Cost: S | M | L (S under a day of agent work, M a few days, L a week or more).
   Recommendation: do | later | skip.
   Check that proves it: <command or count to rerun>.
2. ...
```

The record, `docs/migration-review.md` in the measured repository:

```markdown
# Migration review record: <repository>

Checklist: <ai-migrations commit or date>. Migration: <from> to <to>.

| # | Question | Proposal | Status | Event that shows it | Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Q<n> | <one line> | <status> | <commit, test run or number> | <YYYY-MM-DD> |
```

Status is one of: open, proven, waiting for first use, stopped holding, skipped.

[Spotify]: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-11-06-spotify-honk.md
[Airbnb]: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-01-airbnb-enzyme-to-rtl.md
[Google]: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2025-04-13-google-int64-ids.md

[Uber]: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-migrations/main/cases/2026-04-07-uber-junit4-to-junit5.md
